patterns.rule: Event must happen by a deadline, but proof (filings, official statements, reporting) can arrive after it. Disputes follow when the act and its confirmation straddle the deadline.
Resolves on 'a consensus of credible reporting'. Who counts as credible, and when consensus formed, are open to argument.
Only an official source counts. Disputes follow when the official source is late, silent or contradicts the press.
Title asks about an action (sells, launches, signs, releases) while rules accept an announcement, or the reverse. The gap between saying and doing gets disputed.
Relies on what someone says, wears, mentions or how something looks. Interpretation is subjective.
A date or time in the title with a timezone cut-off (ET/UTC, 11:59 PM). Events near midnight or across timezones get disputed.
Resolves on a specific price feed or candle (exchange, pair, interval). Feed outages, wicks and pair choice get disputed.
Rules spell out a 50-50 or 'other' fallback for unclear cases. Markets that need it often end in a dispute over whether the case is unclear.
Sports result with postponement, cancellation or overtime clauses. Disputes follow schedule changes and stat corrections.
Counts things (tweets, votes, deaths, units) against a threshold. The counting method and source revisions get disputed.
